title: Local decoders for fault-tolerant quantum computation and translation-invariant stabilizer codes
authors: Nathaniel Selub, Aditya Bhardwaj, Ethan Lake
abstract: We construct the first fully spatially local fault-tolerant quantum computer based on topological codes in fewer than four spatial dimensions. Our construction is a two-dimensional architecture that uses only geometrically local quantum and classical operations, bounded-speed classical communication and computation, and a constant density of quantum and classical resources. The core component is a new time-translation-invariant cellular-automaton decoder for the surface code. This decoder preserves logical information for a time stretched-exponential in the code distance and operates continuously during state injection, stabilizer-state preparation, lattice surgery, and transversal readout. We also prove that every translation-invariant topological Pauli stabilizer code is locally decodable under phenomenological noise.
summary: This paper presents a breakthrough in quantum error correction by constructing a fully spatially local, fault-tolerant quantum computer using topological codes in two dimensions. The key innovation is a new time-translation-invariant cellular-automaton decoder that eliminates the need for non-local classical computation. This work significantly advances the feasibility of building scalable quantum hardware by ensuring all necessary operations are geometrically local.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is developing a scalable, fault-tolerant quantum computer based on topological codes that overcomes limitations imposed by classical decoding infrastructure.
main_result: The authors constructed the first fully spatially local fault-tolerant quantum computer based on topological codes in fewer than four spatial dimensions, using a novel time-translation-invariant cellular-automaton decoder.
method: The core method involves designing a local cellular-automaton decoder for the surface code, which is integrated with standard fault-tolerance primitives like lattice surgery and state injection.
model_or_system: The system is a two-dimensional architecture implementing topological codes, specifically focusing on the surface code and general translation-invariant stabilizer codes.
key_observables: Logical error rate, threshold noise rate, and the ability to maintain quantum information integrity under noise.
important_parameters: Code distance ($L$), noise rate ($p$), and the dimensionality ($\le 3$ dimensions).
main_assumptions: Scalability requires constant threshold noise rate, geometrically local interactions, bounded-speed classical communication/computation, and finite resource density.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the 2D fault-tolerant quantum computer using local operations and folded surface code patches. Figure 2 details the toric-code decoding mechanism where error clusters move defects to a corner for annihilation.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem, details the construction of the local CA decoder, proves the general local decodability of translation-invariant codes, and finally presents the full local, 2D fault-tolerant quantum computer realization.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, resource-efficient blueprint for building quantum computers whose error correction mechanisms are entirely local and operate on-chip, which is crucial for physical realization.

Logical operations are performed on a line of surface-code patches decoded by a network of constant-size, noiseless classical processors (local decoders). Each patch is folded along one of its diagonals: stripes indicate spatially overlapping 𝑋- and 𝑍-type stabilizers; qubits overlap in pairs, except along the fold. Defects source messages that grow rightward; within each cluster, these messages cause defects to move monotonically leftward but never beyond the cluster’s initial leftmost defect.
